lessons.title: Our Creator
lessons.notes_html:
Allah Made Everything

  • Allah is the Creator of everything in the world.
  • Allah created the mountains, the trees, the sun, the moon and the stars.
  • Allah also created birds, flowers, animals and all the people.
  • Things made by Allah are made by nature.

Things Made by People

  • Some things are made by people, not by nature.
  • A chair, a pencil, a dice and a sewing machine are made by people.

Key Points

  • Allah is the Creator of everything.
  • Mountains, trees, the sun, a bird and a flower are created by Allah.
  • A chair, a pencil and a dice are made by people.

mcqs.q: Who created everything in the world?
mcqs.why: Allah is the Creator of everything. He created the sun, the moon, the trees, the animals and all the people.

mcqs.q: Which of these is created by Allah?
mcqs.why: A tree grows in nature and is created by Allah. A chair, a pencil and a dice are made by people.

mcqs.q: Which of these things is made by people?
mcqs.why: A chair is made by people. The sun, a bird and a flower are all created by Allah in nature.

mcqs.q: The sun, the moon and the stars are created by whom?
mcqs.why: The sun, the moon and the stars are all created by Allah, because Allah is the Creator of everything.

mcqs.q: Name a thing created by Allah that we can draw.
mcqs.why: In the lesson we draw things created by Allah, such as a tree and a flower. A flower is created by Allah.

mcqs.q: Allah is:
mcqs.why: We learn in this unit that Allah is One. There is only one Allah, and He created all of us.

mcqs.q: The mountains and the trees are made by:
mcqs.why: Mountains and trees are part of nature. They are created by Allah, not made by carpenters, farmers or builders.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT created by nature?
mcqs.why: A sewing machine is made by people. The parrot, the cat and the sunflower are all created by nature.

mcqs.q: A bird is created by:
mcqs.why: A bird is a living thing of nature. All living things, like birds and animals, are created by Allah.

mcqs.q: Allah is:
mcqs.why: Allah is All Merciful. He is kind to all His creation and He takes care of everything in the world.

lessons.title: Prophets
lessons.notes_html:
The Prophets of Allah

  • Allah sent prophets to guide people to the right path.
  • The first Prophet of Allah was Hazrat Adam (A.S).
  • The last Prophet of Allah is Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).
  • No prophet will come after Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).
  • Other prophets are Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S), Hazrat Musa (A.S), Hazrat Daud (A.S) and Hazrat Issa (A.S).

Key Points

  • First Prophet: Hazrat Adam (A.S).
  • Last Prophet: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).
  • We should follow what Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) taught us.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Prophet of Allah?
mcqs.why: Hazrat Adam (A.S) was the first Prophet of Allah. Allah sent him first of all to guide people to the right path.

mcqs.q: Who is the last Prophet of Allah?
mcqs.why: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) is the last Prophet of Allah. No prophet will come after him.

mcqs.q: Will any prophet come after Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H)?
options: No, he is the last Prophet
Yes, only one more will come
mcqs.why: No prophet will come after Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H), because he is the last Prophet of Allah.

mcqs.q: Why did Allah send the prophets?
options: To guide people to the right path
mcqs.why: Allah sent the prophets so that they could guide people to the right path and teach them good things.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) was a:
mcqs.why: Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) was a Prophet of Allah. He is one of the famous prophets named in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a Prophet of Allah?
mcqs.why: Hazrat Musa (A.S) is a Prophet of Allah. The lesson also names Hazrat Daud (A.S) and Hazrat Issa (A.S) as prophets.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Daud (A.S) is a famous:
mcqs.why: Hazrat Daud (A.S) is a famous Prophet of Allah, as told in this lesson about the prophets.

mcqs.q: We should follow the teachings of:
mcqs.why: We should follow what Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) taught us, because he is the last Prophet of Allah.

mcqs.q: Allah sent Hazrat Adam (A.S) first of all as a:
mcqs.why: Allah sent Hazrat Adam (A.S) first of all as a Prophet so that he could guide people to the right path.

mcqs.q: How many prophets will come after the last Prophet?
mcqs.why: No prophet will come after Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H). He is the last Prophet of Allah, so the answer is none.

lessons.title: The Holy Books
lessons.notes_html:
The Holy Books of Allah

  • Allah gave holy books to His prophets for the guidance of people.
  • The Holy Quran was revealed on Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H). It is the holy book of Muslims and the last holy book of Allah.
  • The Bible (Injeel) was revealed on Hazrat Issa (A.S). It is the holy book of Christians.
  • Zabur was revealed on Hazrat Daud (A.S).
  • Torah was revealed on Hazrat Musa (A.S). Zabur and Torah are holy books of the Jews.
  • We must respect all the holy books.

Key Points

  • Holy Quran — Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).
  • Bible (Injeel) — Hazrat Issa (A.S).
  • Zabur — Hazrat Daud (A.S). Torah — Hazrat Musa (A.S).

mcqs.q: The Holy Quran was revealed on:
mcqs.why: The Holy Quran was revealed on Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H). It is the holy book of Muslims and the last holy book of Allah.

mcqs.q: The Bible (Injeel) was revealed on:
mcqs.why: The Bible (Injeel) was revealed on Hazrat Issa (A.S). The Bible is the holy book of Christians.

mcqs.q: Zabur was revealed on:
mcqs.why: Zabur was revealed on Hazrat Daud (A.S). Allah gave this holy book to His prophet for the guidance of people.

mcqs.q: Torah was revealed on:
mcqs.why: Torah was revealed on Hazrat Musa (A.S). Torah is a holy book of the Jews and it guides people to live a good life.

mcqs.q: The holy book of Muslims is:
mcqs.why: The Holy Quran is the holy book of Muslims. It was revealed on Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).

mcqs.q: The holy book of Christians is:
mcqs.why: The Bible (Injeel) is the holy book of Christians. It was revealed on Hazrat Issa (A.S).

mcqs.q: Which is the last holy book of Allah?
mcqs.why: The Holy Quran is the last holy book of Allah Almighty. No holy book came after it.

mcqs.q: Zabur and Torah are holy books of:
mcqs.why: Zabur and Torah are holy books of the Jews. Zabur was given to Hazrat Daud (A.S) and Torah to Hazrat Musa (A.S).

mcqs.q: We must respect:
mcqs.why: We must respect all the holy books, because Allah gave every holy book to guide the people.

mcqs.q: The Holy Quran is the holy book of:
mcqs.why: The Holy Quran is the holy book of Muslims. It was revealed on Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).

lessons.title: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H)
lessons.notes_html:
About Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H)

  • Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) is the last Prophet of Allah.
  • His father was Hazrat Abdullah.
  • His mother was Bibi Aminah.
  • He was born in the city of Makkah.
  • Two qualities of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) were truthfulness and honesty.

Key Points

  • Father: Hazrat Abdullah. Mother: Bibi Aminah.
  • Born in Makkah.
  • He was always truthful and honest.

mcqs.q: The last Prophet of Allah is:
mcqs.why: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) is the last Prophet of Allah. No prophet will come after him.

mcqs.q: The father of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was:
mcqs.why: The father of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was Hazrat Abdullah, as we learn in this lesson.

mcqs.q: The mother of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was:
mcqs.why: The mother of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was Bibi Aminah, as we learn in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was born in the city of:
mcqs.why: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was born in the city of Makkah. Makkah is a holy city for Muslims.

mcqs.q: One quality of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was:
mcqs.why: Truthfulness was a great quality of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H). He always spoke the truth.

mcqs.q: Another quality of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was:
mcqs.why: Honesty was another quality of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H). He was always honest with everyone.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) is the ______ Prophet of Allah.
mcqs.why: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) is the last Prophet of Allah. Hazrat Adam (A.S) was the first Prophet.

mcqs.q: Who was born in the city of Makkah?
mcqs.why: Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H) was born in the city of Makkah. His father was Hazrat Abdullah and his mother was Bibi Aminah.

mcqs.q: Bibi Aminah was the ______ of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).
mcqs.why: Bibi Aminah was the mother of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H), and Hazrat Abdullah was his father.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Abdullah was the ______ of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).
mcqs.why: Hazrat Abdullah was the father of Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H), and Bibi Aminah was his mother.

lessons.title: Worship
lessons.notes_html:
Places of Worship

  • People of every religion go to their own place of worship to pray to God.
  • Muslims pray in a Mosque. In the mosque, Muslims offer Namaz five times a day.
  • Christians pray in a Church.
  • Hindus pray in a Temple.
  • Jews pray in a Synagogue.
  • We should respect the places of worship of all religions.

Key Points

  • Muslims — Mosque. Christians — Church.
  • Hindus — Temple. Jews — Synagogue.

mcqs.q: Muslims pray in a:
mcqs.why: Muslims pray in a mosque. In the mosque, Muslims offer Namaz five times a day and thank Allah for His blessings.

mcqs.q: Christians pray in a:
mcqs.why: Christians pray in a church. People of every religion go to their own place of worship to pray to God.

mcqs.q: Hindus pray in a:
mcqs.why: Hindus pray in a temple. We should respect the places of worship of all religions.

mcqs.q: Jews pray in a:
mcqs.why: Jews pray in a synagogue. It is the place of worship of Jews, where they gather together and pray.

mcqs.q: In the mosque, Muslims offer Namaz:
mcqs.why: In the mosque, Muslims offer Namaz five times a day and thank Allah for His blessings.

mcqs.q: People go to their place of worship to:
mcqs.why: People of every religion go to their own place of worship to pray to God, not to play, buy things or sleep.

mcqs.q: We should respect:
options: The places of worship of all religions
mcqs.why: We should respect the places of worship of all religions, because everyone prays to God in his own place of worship.

mcqs.q: A church is the place of worship of:
mcqs.why: A church is the place of worship of Christians. Muslims pray in a mosque and Hindus pray in a temple.

mcqs.q: A temple is the place of worship of:
mcqs.why: A temple is the place of worship of Hindus. Jews pray in a synagogue and Christians pray in a church.

mcqs.q: A synagogue is the place of worship of:
mcqs.why: A synagogue is the place of worship of Jews, where they gather together and pray to God.

lessons.title: Prayer (Namaz)
lessons.notes_html:
The Five Prayers

  • Muslims offer Namaz (Salah) five times a day.
  • The names of the five Namaz are: 1. Fajr 2. Zuhr 3. Asr 4. Maghrib 5. Isha.
  • The Azaan calls Muslims for Namaz.

Key Points

  • Five Namaz: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.
  • The Azaan calls us for Namaz.

mcqs.q: How many times do Muslims offer Namaz in a day?
mcqs.why: Muslims offer Namaz five times a day. The five Namaz are Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

mcqs.q: The first Namaz of the day is:
mcqs.why: Fajr is the first Namaz of the day. The five Namaz in order are Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

mcqs.q: The last Namaz of the day is:
mcqs.why: Isha is the last Namaz of the day. It comes after Maghrib in the order of the five daily prayers.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the name of a daily Namaz?
mcqs.why: Zuhr is one of the five daily Namaz. Roza, Hajj and Zakat are not names of the daily prayers.

mcqs.q: The call that calls Muslims for Namaz is called:
mcqs.why: The Azaan calls Muslims for Namaz. When we hear the Azaan, we get ready to offer our prayer.

mcqs.q: Namaz is also called:
mcqs.why: Namaz is also called Salah. Muslims offer Salah five times a day: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

mcqs.q: Which Namaz comes after Zuhr?
mcqs.why: Asr comes after Zuhr. The order of the five Namaz is Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

mcqs.q: Which Namaz comes just before Isha?
mcqs.why: Maghrib comes just before Isha. Maghrib is the fourth Namaz and Isha is the fifth and last Namaz of the day.

mcqs.q: Muslims offer Namaz to:
mcqs.why: Muslims offer Namaz to worship Allah. Prayer is our worship, and we offer it five times every day.

mcqs.q: How many names of Namaz are given in this lesson?
mcqs.why: Five names of Namaz are given in this lesson: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. We offer all five every day.

lessons.title: End of Unit 1 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Revision of Unit 1

  • Two things created by nature that we can draw and colour are a tree and a sunflower.
  • Jews: holy book Torah, Prophet Hazrat Musa (A.S), place of worship Synagogue.
  • Christians: holy book Bible, Prophet Hazrat Issa (A.S), place of worship Church.
  • Muslims: holy book Holy Quran, Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H), place of worship Mosque.
  • Sharing food with a friend is a good deed. Being kind and helping others to read are also good deeds.
  • Allah created all of us. Allah is One and Allah is All Merciful.

Key Points

  • Things made by people: sewing machine, pencil, dice and chair.
  • Things created by nature: sunflower, parrot, butterfly, cat and lion.

mcqs.q: Which two things created by nature can we draw and colour?
mcqs.why: A tree and a sunflower are created by nature, so we can draw and colour them. A chair, pencil and dice are made by people.

mcqs.q: The holy book of the Jews is:
mcqs.why: The holy book of the Jews is Torah. Their prophet is Hazrat Musa (A.S) and their place of worship is the Synagogue.

mcqs.q: The Prophet of the Christians is:
mcqs.why: The Prophet of the Christians is Hazrat Issa (A.S). Their holy book is the Bible and their place of worship is the Church.

mcqs.q: The place of worship of Muslims is:
mcqs.why: The place of worship of Muslims is the Mosque. Their holy book is the Holy Quran and their Prophet is Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).

mcqs.q: Sharing your food with a friend who forgot his lunch is:
mcqs.why: Sharing food with a friend is a good deed. Helping others is a good deed, and Allah is pleased with such deeds.

mcqs.q: Which of these is made by people?
mcqs.why: A dice is made by people. The lion, the cat and the butterfly are created by nature, not made by people.

mcqs.q: Allah is:
mcqs.why: Allah is One. Allah created all of us, and the stars are also made by Allah.

mcqs.q: Being kind to a crying child is:
mcqs.why: Being kind to a crying child is a good deed. In the picture the girl is comforting the crying child, which is called being kind.

mcqs.q: Helping a younger child to read is:
mcqs.why: Helping a younger child to read is a good deed. Good deeds make Allah pleased with us.

mcqs.q: The holy book of Muslims is:
mcqs.why: The holy book of Muslims is the Holy Quran. It was revealed on Hazrat Muhammad (P.B.U.H).

lessons.title: The Earth
lessons.notes_html:
Our Earth

  • We all live on the Earth. The Earth is our home.
  • The Earth is covered by land and water.
  • People and animals live on the land. People live in houses and villages, and animals live in fields and forests.
  • Fish and other water animals live in the water.
  • There is more water on the Earth than land.
  • In the picture, land is marked (L) and water is marked (W). Land is coloured green and water is coloured blue.

Key Points

  • People and animals live on land.
  • Fish live in water.
  • There is more water than land on the Earth.

mcqs.q: Who lives on the land?
mcqs.why: People and animals live on the land. People live in houses and villages, while animals live in fields and forests.

mcqs.q: Who lives in the water?
mcqs.why: Fish and other water animals live in the water. The animals living in water cannot live out of water.

mcqs.q: There is more ______ on the Earth.
mcqs.why: There is more water on the Earth. In the picture the big part marked (W) is water and the parts marked (L) are land.

mcqs.q: In the picture of the Earth, land is marked with:
mcqs.why: In the picture, the parts marked (L) are land and the part marked (W) is water.

mcqs.q: In the picture of the Earth, water is marked with:
mcqs.why: In the picture, the part marked (W) is water. The land should be coloured green and the water blue.

mcqs.q: The land in the picture should be coloured:
mcqs.why: The land should be coloured green and the water should be coloured blue in the picture of the Earth.

mcqs.q: The water in the picture should be coloured:
mcqs.why: The water should be coloured blue and the land should be coloured green in the picture of the Earth.

mcqs.q: People live in:
mcqs.why: People live in houses and villages on the land. Animals live in fields and forests, and fish live in water.

mcqs.q: Animals live in:
mcqs.why: Animals live in fields and forests on the land. All of us, people and animals, live on the Earth.

mcqs.q: Water animals cannot live:
mcqs.why: Water animals like fish live in the water. They cannot live out of water, because water is their home.

lessons.title: The Sky
lessons.notes_html:
The Sky at Day and Night

  • In the day we see the sun and the clouds in the sky.
  • The sun looks like a big ball. It shines very brightly and gives us light and heat.
  • At night we see the moon and the stars in the sky.
  • The moon is round like a ball and gives us cool light.
  • The stars are shiny and twinkle in the sky. There are so many stars that we cannot count them.

Key Points

  • Day sky: the sun and the clouds.
  • Night sky: the moon and the stars.

mcqs.q: In the day, we see in the sky:
mcqs.why: In the day we see the sun and the clouds in the sky. The sun gives us light and heat, and the clouds float across the sky.

mcqs.q: The sun gives us:
mcqs.why: The sun gives us light and heat. It shines in the sky in the day and cannot be seen at night.

mcqs.q: At night, we see in the sky:
mcqs.why: At night we see the moon and the stars in the sky. The moon and the stars shine at night and make the sky beautiful.

mcqs.q: "I look like a big ball, shine very brightly in the day and give light." Who am I?
mcqs.why: I am the Sun. The sun shines in the sky in the day, gives us light and heat, and is very hot.

mcqs.q: "I am round like a ball and I shine at night." Who am I?
mcqs.why: I am the Moon. The moon shines in the sky at night, it is round, and it gives us cool light.

mcqs.q: The stars in the night sky:
mcqs.why: Stars twinkle in the sky at night. There are so many of them that they cannot be counted.

mcqs.q: The moon gives us:
mcqs.why: The moon gives us cool light at night. The sun gives us light and heat in the day.

mcqs.q: Can the sun be seen at night?
options: No, the sun is seen only in the day
Yes, it hides behind the moon
mcqs.why: The sun can be seen only in the day. At night we see the moon and the stars in the sky.

mcqs.q: There are so many stars that we:
mcqs.why: There are very many stars in the sky at night, and they are so many that we cannot count them.

mcqs.q: The clouds in the day sky:
mcqs.why: The clouds float across the sky in the day. The sun shines brightly and the stars twinkle at night.

lessons.title: End of Unit 2 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Revision of Unit 2

  • Yes, we all live on the Earth. The Earth is our home.
  • No, we do not see the sun at night. At night we see the moon and the stars.
  • The sun shines very brightly and it is very hot. Nobody can live on the sun.
  • Because of the sun's heat, our Earth stays warm and plants grow.
  • Poem 1: "I see the moon, and the moon sees me." Poem 2: "Twinkle twinkle little star."

Key Points

  • The Earth is our home.
  • The sun is seen in the day; the moon and stars are seen at night.

mcqs.q: Do we live on the Earth?
options: No, we live on the sun
Yes, the Earth is our home
No, we live on the moon
No, we live in the sky
mcqs.why: Yes, we all live on the Earth, because the Earth is our home and our houses, schools and fields are all here.

mcqs.q: Do we see the sun at night?
options: Yes, the sun shines at night
Yes, the sun and moon shine together
No, at night we see the moon and the stars
mcqs.why: No, the sun can be seen only in the day. At night we see the moon and the stars in the sky.

mcqs.q: The sun shines:
mcqs.why: Yes, the sun shines very brightly, and its light is so strong that we cannot look straight at it.

mcqs.q: Can anyone live on the sun?
options: No, it is too hot and has no water or air
mcqs.why: No, nobody can live on the sun. The sun is so hot, and there is no water and no air there, so life is not possible there.

mcqs.q: The poem "Twinkle twinkle little star" is about:
mcqs.why: The poem "Twinkle twinkle little star, how I wonder what you are" is about a star in the night sky.

mcqs.q: The poem "I see the moon, and the moon sees me" is about:
mcqs.why: Poem 1 says, "I see the moon, and the moon sees me, God bless the moon and God bless me." It is about the moon.

mcqs.q: In the night sky, we can see:
options: The round moon and the twinkling stars
mcqs.why: In the night sky we can see the round moon and the twinkling stars, which look very beautiful.

mcqs.q: The light of the sun is so strong that we:
mcqs.why: The sun shines very brightly, and its light is so strong that we cannot look straight at it.

mcqs.q: Because of the heat of the sun:
options: The Earth stays warm and plants grow
mcqs.why: The sun is very hot, and it is because of its heat that our Earth stays warm and plants grow.

mcqs.q: When the sky is clear at night, we see:
mcqs.why: At night many stars can be seen twinkling in the sky, especially when the sky is clear.

lessons.title: Who Am I?
lessons.notes_html:
Telling About Myself

  • This is a practice lesson. In this lesson, every child tells about himself or herself.
  • We tell our name, our age and the class we study in.
  • We also tell what we like and what we do not like.

A Model Answer

  • My name is Ali. I am six years old.
  • I study in class one.
  • I like to read and play cricket. I do not like to fight with others.
  • Every child will write his or her own name, age and class.

Key Points

  • We introduce ourselves by our name, age and class.
  • We also tell our likes and dislikes.

mcqs.q: In this lesson, we tell others about:
mcqs.why: In this lesson every child tells about himself or herself: his name, his age, his class and his likes and dislikes.

mcqs.q: In the model answer, the boy's name is:
mcqs.why: In the model answer the boy says, "My name is Ali." Every child will write his or her own name in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Ali is ______ years old.
mcqs.why: In the model answer Ali says, "I am six years old." Every child will write his or her own age.

mcqs.q: Ali studies in class:
mcqs.why: In the model answer Ali says, "I study in class one." He is a student of Class 1, like you.

mcqs.q: Ali likes to:
mcqs.why: Ali says, "I like to read and play cricket." Reading and playing cricket are good things to like.

mcqs.q: Ali does not like to:
mcqs.why: Ali says, "I do not like to fight with others." Fighting with others is a bad habit, so he does not like it.

mcqs.q: When we introduce ourselves, we first tell our:
mcqs.why: When we introduce ourselves, we first tell our name, then our age and the class we study in.

mcqs.q: "My name is ______" tells our:
mcqs.why: The sentence "My name is" tells our name. For age we say "I am six years old" and for class "I study in class one."

mcqs.q: To tell our age, we say:
mcqs.why: To tell our age we say, "I am six years old." The other sentences tell our name, our class and our liking.

mcqs.q: In this lesson, every child writes:
options: His or her own name, age and class
mcqs.why: Every child will write his or her own name, age and class in this lesson, because it tells about himself or herself.

lessons.title: My Body
lessons.notes_html:
Our Five Senses

  • We have five senses. We do five things with our body parts.
  • We see with our eyes. We have two eyes.
  • We hear with our ears. We have two ears.
  • We smell with our nose.
  • We taste with our tongue. The tongue tells us sweet, salty, sour or bitter.
  • We touch and feel with our hands. We have two hands.

Match the Senses

  • Eye — rainbow (we see it). Ear — bell (we hear it).
  • Nose — flower (we smell it). Tongue — ice-cream (we taste it). Hand — feather (we touch it).

Key Points

  • Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes, hands touch.

mcqs.q: We see with our:
mcqs.why: We see with our eyes. We have two eyes, and with them we see all things and colours around us.

mcqs.q: We hear sounds with our:
mcqs.why: We hear with our ears. We have two ears, and with them we hear sounds and voices, like the sound of a bell.

mcqs.q: We smell with our:
mcqs.why: We smell with our nose. With our nose we feel the sweet smell of flowers and the smell of other things.

mcqs.q: We taste with our:
mcqs.why: We taste with our tongue. With our tongue we know whether a thing is sweet, salty, sour or bitter.

mcqs.q: We touch and feel with our:
mcqs.why: We touch and feel with our hands. We have two hands, and with them we can feel soft and hard things.

mcqs.q: The eye goes with the:
mcqs.why: The eye goes with the rainbow, because we see with our eyes. We hear the bell, smell the flower and touch the feather.

mcqs.q: The ear goes with the:
mcqs.why: The ear goes with the bell, because we hear with our ears. We see the rainbow and taste the ice-cream.

mcqs.q: The nose goes with the:
mcqs.why: The nose goes with the flower, because we smell with our nose. We feel the sweet smell of flowers with our nose.

mcqs.q: The tongue goes with the:
mcqs.why: The tongue goes with the ice-cream, because we taste with our tongue. We touch the feather with our hands.

mcqs.q: How many senses do we have?
mcqs.why: We have five senses: we see, hear, smell, taste and touch. These five things are done by our five senses.

lessons.title: Keeping Ourselves Clean
lessons.notes_html:
Things That Keep Us Clean

  • Many things help us to keep clean.
  • A toothbrush and toothpaste clean our teeth.
  • Soap washes our hands and body. Shampoo washes our hair.
  • A comb makes our hair neat. A towel dries our body.
  • A nail cutter cuts our nails. A bucket carries water for a bath.
  • By using these things we stay neat, clean and healthy.

Key Points

  • Toothbrush, soap, bucket, comb, towel, nail cutter, toothpaste and shampoo keep us clean.

mcqs.q: We brush our teeth with a:
mcqs.why: We brush our teeth with a toothbrush. A comb is for hair, a towel dries our body and a nail cutter cuts our nails.

mcqs.q: We wash our hands and body with:
mcqs.why: We wash our hands and body with soap. Shampoo washes our hair and toothpaste cleans our teeth.

mcqs.q: We cut our nails with a:
mcqs.why: We cut our nails with a nail cutter. Keeping our nails short and clean is part of keeping ourselves clean.

mcqs.q: We dry our body after a bath with a:
mcqs.why: We dry our body with a towel after a bath. A comb makes our hair neat and soap washes our body.

mcqs.q: We wash our hair with:
mcqs.why: We wash our hair with shampoo. Toothpaste is for our teeth and a towel is for drying our body.

mcqs.q: We make our hair neat with a:
mcqs.why: We comb our hair with a comb to make it neat. A nail cutter cuts nails and a toothbrush cleans teeth.

mcqs.q: Toothpaste is used to clean our:
mcqs.why: Toothpaste is used with a toothbrush to clean our teeth. We clean our teeth in the morning and at night.

mcqs.q: Water for a bath is carried in a:
mcqs.why: Water for a bath is carried in a bucket. The bucket is one of the things that help us keep clean.

mcqs.q: By using clean things, we stay:
mcqs.why: By using things like soap, a toothbrush and a towel, we stay neat, clean and healthy.

mcqs.q: Which of these helps us keep clean?
mcqs.why: Soap helps us keep clean because we wash our hands and body with it. A ball, a kite and a toy car are toys for playing.

lessons.title: Good Manners
lessons.notes_html:
Good Manners of Sana and Ali

  • Sana and Ali greet their parents by saying Salaam.
  • They wear clean uniforms. They say a prayer before having breakfast.
  • Sana says "Please" when she asks for a chappati and "Thank you" when her father gives it to her.
  • Ali helps his friends to read. Sana helps an old man cross the street.
  • They also respect their elders.

Good Qualities

  • Good qualities: I speak politely, I am honest, I am kind to animals, I put litter in the bin, I help the poor, I help others.
  • Not good qualities: I write on the wall, I sleep in the classroom.
  • Good qualities make me a good person and my friends like me.

Key Points

  • Say Salaam, Please and Thank you.
  • Help others and respect elders.

mcqs.q: Sana and Ali greet their parents by saying:
mcqs.why: Sana and Ali greet their parents by saying Salaam. Greeting our parents with Salaam is a good manner.

mcqs.q: When Sana asks for a chappati, she says:
mcqs.why: Sana says "Please" when she asks for a chappati. Saying please when we ask for something is a good manner.

mcqs.q: When her father gives her the chappati, Sana says:
mcqs.why: Sana says "Thank you" when her father gives her the chappati. We should thank the person who gives us something.

mcqs.q: Before having breakfast, Sana and Ali:
mcqs.why: Sana and Ali say a prayer before having breakfast. They also wear clean uniforms and greet their parents.

mcqs.q: Ali helps his friends to:
mcqs.why: Ali helps his friends to read. Helping our friends in reading is a good manner and a good deed.

mcqs.q: Sana helps an old man to:
mcqs.why: Sana helps an old man cross the street. Helping old people is a good manner, and we should respect our elders.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a good quality?
options: I throw litter on the ground
mcqs.why: Speaking politely is a good quality. Writing on the wall and sleeping in the classroom are not good qualities.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a good quality?
mcqs.why: Writing on the wall is not a good quality. Being honest, helping others and putting litter in the bin are good qualities.

mcqs.q: Good qualities make me:
options: A good person and my friends like me
mcqs.why: Good qualities make me a good person and my friends like me, as we say at the end of this lesson.

mcqs.q: We should put litter in:
mcqs.why: Putting litter in the bin is a good quality. We should never throw litter in the street or on the floor.

lessons.title: Our Favourite Games
lessons.notes_html:
The Game of Ludo

  • In Ludo, every player chooses a coloured playing piece.
  • Players take turns to throw the dice.
  • A playing piece comes out at the throw of a six.
  • We move the playing piece along the track as many spaces as the number shown on the dice.
  • The first person to move all four pieces into the home area wins.

Games We Like

  • The games we like to play are cricket, football and ludo.
  • My favourite game is cricket.

Key Points

  • Ludo is played with playing pieces and a dice.
  • A piece comes out on a six. The first to take all pieces home wins.

mcqs.q: In Ludo, we throw a:
mcqs.why: In Ludo, players take turns to throw the dice. The playing piece moves as many spaces as the number shown on the dice.

mcqs.q: In Ludo, a playing piece comes out at the throw of a:
mcqs.why: A playing piece moves out from the corner at the throw of a six. Then it moves along the track by the dice number.

mcqs.q: The winner of Ludo is the first person to:
options: Move all four pieces into the home area
mcqs.why: The first person to move all four pieces into the home area wins the game of Ludo.

mcqs.q: We move the playing piece as many spaces as:
options: The number shown on the dice
mcqs.why: We move the playing piece along the track the number of spaces shown on the dice, no more and no less.

mcqs.q: In Ludo, every player first chooses a:
mcqs.why: In Ludo, every player chooses a coloured playing piece and then takes turns to throw the dice.

mcqs.q: Players throw the dice:
mcqs.why: In Ludo, players take turns to throw the dice. One player throws, then the next player throws.

mcqs.q: Which games do the children like to play?
mcqs.why: The games we like to play are cricket, football and ludo, as told in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a game?
mcqs.why: Cricket is a game we like to play. Bathing, brushing and sweeping are daily work, not games.

mcqs.q: In the lesson, my favourite game is:
mcqs.why: In the lesson the child says, "My favourite game is cricket." Every child may have his or her own favourite game.

mcqs.q: Ludo is played with:
mcqs.why: Ludo is played with coloured playing pieces and a dice. A bat and ball are for cricket and a rope is for skipping.

lessons.title: What I Want to Be?
lessons.notes_html:
People and Their Work

  • A teacher teaches children reading, writing and good things in the school.
  • Farmers do farming in the fields. They grow crops, from which we get grain and vegetables to eat.
  • A shopkeeper sells things in his shop. We buy things of daily use from him.
  • A nurse looks after sick people. She gives medicine to the patients and helps the doctor.
  • A doctor treats patients and makes them well again.

When I Grow Up

  • When I grow up I would like to be a teacher, because I like to teach children and tell them good things.
  • To find the most preferred work, ask every student and write the names in the box of that work. The work with the most names is the most preferred work.

Key Points

  • Teacher teaches, farmer grows crops, shopkeeper sells things, nurse and doctor care for the sick.

mcqs.q: A teacher:
mcqs.why: A teacher teaches students reading, writing and good things in the school, as we see in this lesson.

mcqs.q: A farmer:
mcqs.why: Farmers do farming in the fields. They grow crops in the land, from which we get grain and vegetables to eat.

mcqs.q: From a shopkeeper, we buy:
mcqs.why: From the shopkeeper we buy things of daily use, such as food items, copies and pencils.

mcqs.q: A nurse:
mcqs.why: A nurse looks after the sick people. She gives medicine to the patients in the hospital and helps the doctor.

mcqs.q: A doctor:
options: Treats patients and gives them medicine
mcqs.why: A doctor treats patients. He gives medicine to sick people and makes them well again so that they become healthy.

mcqs.q: We get grain and vegetables from the work of:
mcqs.why: Farmers grow crops in the land, from which we get grain and vegetables to eat. So we get them from the work of farmers.

mcqs.q: A nurse helps the:
mcqs.why: A nurse gives medicine to the patients in the hospital and helps the doctor in his work.

mcqs.q: To find the students' most preferred work, we:
options: Ask every student and write the names in boxes
mcqs.why: Ask every student what work he or she wants to do, and write the name in the box of that work, like teachers, doctors, farmers, pilots or shopkeepers.

mcqs.q: The most preferred work is the work:
options: Whose box has the most names
mcqs.why: The work whose box has the most names will be the students' most preferred work.

mcqs.q: In the lesson, the child wants to be a:
mcqs.why: In the lesson the child says, "When I grow up I would like to be a teacher, because I like to teach children."

lessons.title: End of Unit 3 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Revision of Unit 3

  • I have two eyes and two hands. I smell and breathe with my nose.
  • I wash my hands many times a day. I take a bath once a day. I clean my teeth two times a day and comb my hair two times a day.
  • Tastes: apple is sweet, chips are salty, karela is bitter, lemon is sour.
  • Games: cricket — bat and ball; hockey — stick and ball; hopscotch — flat stone; skipping — skipping rope.
  • To become what we want to be: study in school, do homework and work hard.

Key Points

  • Clean teeth two times a day, take a bath once a day.
  • Apple sweet, chips salty, karela bitter, lemon sour.

mcqs.q: How many times do we clean our teeth in a day?
mcqs.why: I clean my teeth two times in a day, in the morning and at night before sleeping. Cleaning the teeth keeps them strong and clean.

mcqs.q: How many times do we take a bath in a day?
mcqs.why: I take a bath once in a day. Bathing every day keeps the body clean, and we feel fresh and healthy.

mcqs.q: The taste of an apple is:
mcqs.why: The taste of an apple is sweet. An apple is a good fruit, and we taste its sweetness with our tongue.

mcqs.q: The taste of chips is:
mcqs.why: The taste of chips is salty. Salt is mixed in chips, so their taste is salty.

mcqs.q: The taste of karela is:
mcqs.why: The taste of karela is bitter. Karela is a vegetable which is bitter, but it is very good for health.

mcqs.q: The taste of lemon is:
mcqs.why: The taste of lemon is sour. Lemon is a sour fruit, and sherbet is also made from it.

mcqs.q: Cricket is played with:
mcqs.why: Cricket is played with a bat and a ball. The player hits the ball with the bat and makes runs.

mcqs.q: Hockey is played with:
mcqs.why: Hockey is played with a stick and a ball. The players move the ball forward with the stick and try to make a goal.

mcqs.q: Skipping is played with:
mcqs.why: Skipping is played with a skipping rope. Jumping over the turning rope keeps the body strong and healthy.

mcqs.q: Hopscotch is played with:
mcqs.why: Hopscotch is played with a flat stone. The stone is thrown into the boxes drawn on the ground, and the game is played by hopping on one leg.

lessons.title: My Family
lessons.notes_html:
Sana's Family

  • This lesson tells about Sana's family. Every child will write about his or her own family.
  • Sana's father's name is Mr. Ahmed.
  • Sana's mother's name is Mrs. Nida Ahmed.
  • Sana has one brother and one sister.
  • Their names are Ali and Hina.

Key Points

  • A family has a father, a mother, brothers and sisters.
  • We should know the names of our family members.

mcqs.q: Sana's father's name is:
mcqs.why: Sana's father's name is Mr. Ahmed and her mother's name is Mrs. Nida Ahmed, as told in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Sana's mother's name is:
mcqs.why: Sana's mother's name is Mrs. Nida Ahmed. Her father's name is Mr. Ahmed.

mcqs.q: Sana has:
mcqs.why: Sana has one brother and one sister. Their names are Ali and Hina.

mcqs.q: Sana's brother and sister are:
mcqs.why: The names of Sana's brother and sister are Ali and Hina. Ali is her brother and Hina is her sister.

mcqs.q: This lesson, "My Family", tells about:
mcqs.why: This lesson tells about Sana's family. Every child will write the names of his or her own family members.

mcqs.q: How many brothers does Sana have?
mcqs.why: Sana has one brother. His name is Ali. She also has one sister, whose name is Hina.

mcqs.q: How many sisters does Sana have?
mcqs.why: Sana has one sister. Her name is Hina. She also has one brother, whose name is Ali.

mcqs.q: Hina is Sana's:
mcqs.why: Hina is Sana's sister. Ali is Sana's brother, and Mr. Ahmed and Mrs. Nida Ahmed are her parents.

mcqs.q: Ali is Sana's:
mcqs.why: Ali is Sana's brother. Hina is her sister, and together they make Sana's family with their father and mother.

mcqs.q: In this lesson, every child will write:
options: The names of his or her own family members
mcqs.why: Every child will write the names of his or her own family members, like Sana wrote about her family.

lessons.title: Relationships at Home
lessons.notes_html:
What Our Family Does for Us

  • Mother cooks food for us and keeps us clean and healthy. If she did not cook, we would be hungry.
  • Father helps us with our homework and reads stories to us at night. If he did not read stories, we would be sad.
  • Hina, the sister, plays with me. If she did not play, I would have no one to play with.
  • Ali, the brother, plays with me and helps me in reading. If he did not help, reading would be difficult for me.

Key Points

  • Every family member helps us in his or her own way.
  • We should love and thank our family.

mcqs.q: Who cooks food for the family in this lesson?
mcqs.why: Mother cooks food for us and keeps us clean and healthy. If she did not cook, we would be hungry.

mcqs.q: Father helps us with our:
mcqs.why: Father helps us with our homework and reads stories to us at night, as told in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Father reads ______ to us at night.
mcqs.why: Father reads stories to us at night. If he did not read stories, we would be sad.

mcqs.q: Hina, the sister, does this for Sana:
mcqs.why: Hina plays with Sana. If she did not play, Sana would have no one to play with at home.

mcqs.q: Ali, the brother, helps Sana in:
mcqs.why: Ali plays with Sana and helps her in reading. If he did not help, reading would be difficult for her.

mcqs.q: If mother did not cook food, we would be:
mcqs.why: Mother cooks food for us. If she did not cook, we would be hungry, so we should thank her.

mcqs.q: Mother keeps us:
mcqs.why: Mother cooks food for us and keeps us clean and healthy. This is what mother does for us at home.

mcqs.q: Who plays with Sana at home?
options: Her brother Ali and her sister Hina
mcqs.why: Hina plays with Sana, and Ali also plays with her and helps her in reading. They are her brother and sister.

mcqs.q: If father did not read stories at night, we would be:
mcqs.why: Father reads stories to us at night. If he did not read stories, we would be sad.

mcqs.q: Every family member:
options: Helps us in his or her own way
mcqs.why: Mother cooks, father helps in homework and reads stories, sister plays and brother helps in reading. Every member helps in his or her own way.

lessons.title: Our Home
lessons.notes_html:
Rooms of Our Home

  • Sana's family lives in a flat.
  • The home has a sitting room, two bedrooms, a kitchen and a bathroom.
  • Sitting room: chair, table, T.V, carpet, fan and window.
  • Bedroom: bed, pillow, blanket and cupboard.
  • Kitchen: stove, pots and pans, spoon and plates.

Keeping the Home Clean

  • We keep our home clean by sweeping every day, mopping the floor and dusting the furniture.
  • We also clean the carpet, wash the dishes and throw litter in the bin.
  • All the family members should do these things together.

Key Points

  • We cook in the kitchen and sleep in the bedroom.
  • We always keep our home clean.

mcqs.q: Sana's family lives in a:
mcqs.why: Sana's family lives in a flat. Their home has a sitting room, two bedrooms, a kitchen and a bathroom.

mcqs.q: How many bedrooms are there in the home?
mcqs.why: The home has two bedrooms, along with a sitting room, a kitchen and a bathroom.

mcqs.q: We cook food in the:
mcqs.why: We cook food in the kitchen. The stove, pots and pans, spoon and plates are kept in the kitchen.

mcqs.q: We sleep in the:
mcqs.why: We sleep in the bedroom. The bed, pillow, blanket and cupboard are in the bedroom.

mcqs.q: A stove is found in the:
mcqs.why: A stove is found in the kitchen, with pots and pans, a spoon and plates. We cook our food on the stove.

mcqs.q: A bed, a pillow and a blanket are in the:
mcqs.why: A bed, a pillow, a blanket and a cupboard are in the bedroom. We sleep on the bed with a pillow and a blanket.

mcqs.q: Guests sit in the:
mcqs.why: Guests sit in the sitting room. The chair, table, T.V, carpet, fan and window are in the sitting room.

mcqs.q: To keep the home clean, we:
options: Sweep and mop the floor every day
mcqs.why: To keep the home clean we sweep every day, mop the floor, dust the furniture and wash the dishes.

mcqs.q: Litter in the home should be thrown in:
mcqs.why: We throw litter in the bin and put the washed dishes in their place. This keeps our home clean.

mcqs.q: The home should be kept clean by:
mcqs.why: All the family members should do the cleaning things together, so that the home stays clean and healthy.

lessons.title: Life and Family History
lessons.notes_html:
Important Events of Ali's Life

  • 2006: Ali was born.
  • 2007: Ali started walking.
  • 2010: Ali started school.
  • 2011: His baby sister Hina was born.
  • 2013: The whole family went for a picnic to the seaside.
  • Every child will write the events of his or her own life with his or her own years.

Key Points

  • A life history tells the important events of our life in order.

mcqs.q: Ali was born in:
mcqs.why: Ali was born in 2006. This was the first important event of his life in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Ali started walking in:
mcqs.why: Ali started walking in 2007, one year after he was born in 2006.

mcqs.q: Ali started school in:
mcqs.why: Ali started school in 2010. After that, his baby sister Hina was born in 2011.

mcqs.q: Ali's baby sister Hina was born in:
mcqs.why: Ali's baby sister Hina was born in 2011. Ali had started school in 2010, before his sister was born.

mcqs.q: In 2013, the whole family went:
options: For a picnic to the seaside
mcqs.why: In 2013 the whole family went for a picnic to the seaside. This is one of the important events of Ali's life.

mcqs.q: This lesson tells about:
mcqs.why: This lesson tells about the important events of our life, like being born, starting to walk and starting school.

mcqs.q: The first event in Ali's life was:
mcqs.why: The first event in Ali's life was that he was born in 2006. Then he started walking in 2007.

mcqs.q: Which event came after Ali started school?
options: His baby sister Hina was born
mcqs.why: Ali started school in 2010 and his baby sister Hina was born in 2011, so her birth came after he started school.

mcqs.q: Every child will write the events of:
mcqs.why: Every child will write the events of his or her own life with his or her own years, like Ali's life in the lesson.

mcqs.q: A family history tells us about:
options: The important events of our family's life
mcqs.why: A life and family history tells us about the important events of our family's life in the order they happened.

lessons.title: The Food We Eat
lessons.notes_html:
Our Meals

  • For breakfast my family eats eggs, paratha and milk.
  • For lunch my family eats rice and daal.
  • For dinner my family eats roti and vegetables.
  • The vegetables I like to eat are potatoes and carrots. The fruits I like to eat are apples and bananas. I like to drink milk.

Before, While and After Eating

  • Before eating we wash our hands and thank God by saying a prayer.
  • While eating we eat slowly, we do not talk with our mouth full, and we eat all the food on our plate.
  • After eating we thank Allah for the food He gave us and wash our hands.

Key Points

  • Wash hands before and after eating.
  • Eat slowly and do not talk with your mouth full.

mcqs.q: For breakfast, the family eats:
mcqs.why: For breakfast my family eats eggs, paratha and milk. For lunch we eat rice and daal and for dinner roti and vegetables.

mcqs.q: For lunch, the family eats:
mcqs.why: For lunch my family eats rice and daal. Breakfast is eggs, paratha and milk, and dinner is roti and vegetables.

mcqs.q: For dinner, the family eats:
mcqs.why: For dinner my family eats roti and vegetables. Lunch is rice and daal in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Before eating, we:
options: Wash our hands only after eating
Wash our hands and say a prayer
mcqs.why: Before eating we wash our hands and thank God by saying a prayer. Clean hands keep us safe from germs.

mcqs.q: While eating, we should:
mcqs.why: While eating we eat slowly, we do not talk with our mouth full, and we eat all the food on our plate.

mcqs.q: We should not:
mcqs.why: We should not talk with our mouth full while eating. We should eat slowly and eat all the food on our plate.

mcqs.q: After eating, we:
options: Thank Allah and wash our hands
mcqs.why: After eating we thank Allah for the food He gave us and wash our hands. This is a good habit.

mcqs.q: The fruits liked in this lesson are:
mcqs.why: The fruits I like to eat are apples and bananas. The vegetables I like are potatoes and carrots.

mcqs.q: The vegetables liked in this lesson are:
mcqs.why: The vegetables I like to eat are potatoes and carrots, as told in this lesson about the food we eat.

mcqs.q: We should eat:
options: Only the food we like most
All the food on our plate
mcqs.why: While eating, we eat all the food on our plate. We should not waste the food given to us.

lessons.title: End of Unit 4 Exercise

lessons.title: Our Neighbourhood
lessons.notes_html:
Places in Our Neighbourhood

  • The place around our home where many people live together is our neighbourhood.
  • The people who live near us are called our neighbours.
  • In a neighbourhood there is a shop, a school, a mosque, a park and lots of houses.
  • There is also a health centre in the neighbourhood.

Key Points

  • Our neighbourhood has shops, a school, a mosque, a park, a health centre and houses.

mcqs.q: The people who live near our home are called our:
mcqs.why: The people who live together near our homes in a neighbourhood are called neighbours.

mcqs.q: Which of these places is in our neighbourhood?
mcqs.why: In a neighbourhood there is a school, a health centre, a park, a mosque and lots of shops and houses.

mcqs.q: Children go to study at the:
mcqs.why: Children go to study at the school in the neighbourhood. We buy things from a shop and play in the park.

mcqs.q: We buy things of daily use from a:
mcqs.why: We buy things of daily use from a shop in our neighbourhood, like food items, copies and pencils.

mcqs.q: We play with our friends in the:
mcqs.why: We play in the park in our neighbourhood. There are swings and slides in the park.

mcqs.q: We pray in the:
mcqs.why: We pray in the mosque in our neighbourhood. Muslims come to the mosque to pray when they hear the Azaan.

mcqs.q: For treatment when we are sick, we go to the:
mcqs.why: In a neighbourhood there is also a health centre, where we go for treatment when we are sick or hurt.

mcqs.q: People live in:
mcqs.why: People live in houses in the neighbourhood. Many people live together there and are called neighbours.

mcqs.q: Our neighbourhood is:
options: A place far from our home
The place around our home where many people live together
mcqs.why: In a neighbourhood many people live together near each other, with a school, a park, a mosque and shops around their homes.

mcqs.q: Neighbours live:
mcqs.why: Neighbours live together in one area around their homes. We should live with them with love and peace.

lessons.title: Shops in Our Neighbourhood
lessons.notes_html:
Shops and the Things They Sell

  • Apples are sold at a fruit shop.
  • We buy eggs from a grocer. We also buy milk and sugar from the grocery shop.
  • Meat is sold at a meat shop.
  • I buy pencils from a book shop. Books and copies are also sold there.
  • Potatoes and carrots are bought from a vegetable shop.
