  • A fish has no legs. Its body is covered with scales. It swims.
  • A parrot has 2 legs and feathers. It flies.
  • A frog has 4 legs. It hops and swims. A goat, a horse and a camel have 4 legs and hair.

Key Points

  • All these animals have 2 eyes.
  • Animals move in different ways: walk, fly, swim and hop.

mcqs.q: A fish has:
mcqs.why: A fish has no legs. Its body is covered with scales and it swims in water.

mcqs.q: A cockroach has:
mcqs.why: A cockroach has 6 legs and 2 eyes. Its body is covered with skin, a hard shell, and it walks.

mcqs.q: A hen's body is covered with:
mcqs.why: A hen has 2 legs and 2 eyes, and its body is covered with feathers. It walks and flies.

mcqs.q: A fish's body is covered with:
mcqs.why: A fish has no legs, its body is covered with scales, and it swims in the water.

mcqs.q: A parrot moves by:
mcqs.why: A parrot has 2 legs and feathers, and it flies. A hen walks and flies, and a fish swims.

mcqs.q: A frog moves by:
mcqs.why: A frog has 4 legs and it hops and swims. A horse walks and runs, and a parrot flies.

mcqs.q: A cow has:
mcqs.why: A cow has 4 legs and 2 eyes. Its body is covered with hair and skin, and it walks.

mcqs.q: All the animals in this lesson have:
mcqs.why: Cow, hen, cockroach, goat, horse, fish, parrot, frog and camel all have 2 eyes, but their legs and body covers are different.

mcqs.q: A horse moves by:
mcqs.why: A horse has 4 legs and hair, and it walks and runs. A frog hops and swims, and a fish only swims.

mcqs.q: A camel's body is covered with:
mcqs.why: A camel has 4 legs and 2 eyes, and its body is covered with hair. It walks, like the cow and the goat.

lessons.title: The Food Animals Eat
lessons.notes_html:
Matching Animals with Their Food

  • A cat likes to eat meat. Cats, dogs and lions eat meat.
  • A cow likes to eat grass. Sheep, cows and goats eat grass.
  • A dog likes to chew a bone.
  • A fish likes to eat small worms found in water.
  • A hen likes to eat grains. Hens peck grains and seeds from the ground.
  • A parrot likes to eat fruits and vegetables, like chillies and guavas.

Key Points

  • Some animals eat meat and some animals eat grass.
  • Every animal needs food to live.

mcqs.q: A cat likes to eat:
mcqs.why: A cat likes to eat meat. Cats, dogs and lions eat meat, while cows and goats eat grass.

mcqs.q: A cow likes to eat:
mcqs.why: A cow likes to eat grass. Sheep, cows and goats eat grass, and they need food to live.

mcqs.q: A dog likes to chew a:
mcqs.why: A dog likes to chew a bone. Dogs eat meat, and a bone is their favourite food.

mcqs.q: A fish likes to eat:
mcqs.why: A fish likes to eat small worms found in water. Fish live in water and find their food there.

mcqs.q: A hen likes to eat:
mcqs.why: A hen likes to eat grains. Hens peck grains and seeds from the ground and eat them.

mcqs.q: A parrot likes to eat:
mcqs.why: A parrot likes to eat fruits and vegetables. Parrots eat chillies, guavas and other fruits with great liking.

mcqs.q: Lions eat:
mcqs.why: Cats, dogs and lions eat meat. Cows, sheep and goats eat grass.

mcqs.q: Goats and sheep eat:
mcqs.why: Sheep, cows and goats eat grass. They need food to live, like all animals.

mcqs.q: Hens peck ______ from the ground and eat them.
mcqs.why: Hens peck grains and seeds from the ground and eat them. Grains are the food of a hen.

mcqs.q: Parrots eat ______ with great liking.
mcqs.why: Parrots eat chillies, guavas and other fruits with great liking. Fruits and vegetables are the food of a parrot.

lessons.title: Homes Where Animals Live
lessons.notes_html:
Homes of Animals

  • A bird's home is called a nest.
  • Birds make their nests in trees and keep their babies in them.
  • A rabbit's home is called a burrow.
  • A rabbit makes its burrow by digging in the ground. Living in it keeps it safe.

Key Points

  • Bird — nest in a tree. Rabbit — burrow in the ground.

mcqs.q: A bird's home is called a:
mcqs.why: A bird's home is called a nest. Birds make their nests in trees and keep their babies in them.

mcqs.q: Birds make their nests in:
mcqs.why: Birds make their nests in trees and keep their babies in them. A rabbit makes its home in the ground.

mcqs.q: A rabbit's home is called a:
mcqs.why: A rabbit's home is called a burrow. A rabbit makes its burrow by digging in the ground.

mcqs.q: A rabbit makes its burrow by:
mcqs.why: A rabbit makes its burrow by digging in the ground, and living in it keeps it safe.

mcqs.q: Birds keep their ______ in the nest.
mcqs.why: Birds make their nests in trees and keep their babies in them. The nest is the home of a bird.

mcqs.q: Living in the burrow keeps the rabbit:
mcqs.why: A rabbit makes its burrow by digging in the ground, and living in it keeps it safe from danger.

mcqs.q: A nest is made by a:
mcqs.why: A nest is made by a bird in a tree. A rabbit makes a burrow and a fish lives in water.

mcqs.q: A burrow is made in the:
mcqs.why: A burrow is made in the ground by a rabbit. A nest is made by a bird in a tree.

mcqs.q: Where does a bird live?
mcqs.why: A bird lives in a nest, which it makes in a tree. It keeps its babies in the nest.

mcqs.q: Where does a rabbit live?
mcqs.why: A rabbit lives in a burrow, which it makes by digging in the ground. The burrow keeps it safe.

lessons.title: Farm, Pet and Wild Animals
lessons.notes_html:
Pet and Wild Animals

  • A cat is a pet animal. It lives at home. It likes to eat meat and drink milk.
  • We can play with a cat and take care of it by giving it food and water.
  • A lion is a wild animal. It lives in the jungle and eats meat.
  • We cannot play with a lion and cannot take care of it at home, because it is dangerous.
  • Sana and Ali can keep a cat at home. The pet cat's name is Moti. She likes milk and meat.

Key Points

  • Pet animals live at home. Wild animals live in the jungle.

mcqs.q: A cat is a:
mcqs.why: A cat is a pet animal. It lives at home, and we can play with it and take care of it.

mcqs.q: A lion is a:
mcqs.why: A lion is a wild animal. It lives in the jungle, and we cannot play with it or keep it at home.

mcqs.q: A lion lives in the:
mcqs.why: A lion lives in the jungle. It eats meat and it is a dangerous wild animal.

mcqs.q: We can keep at home a:
mcqs.why: Sana and Ali can keep a cat at home, because a cat is a pet animal. A lion is wild and dangerous.

mcqs.q: We cannot play with a:
mcqs.why: We cannot play with a lion, as it is a dangerous wild animal. We can play with a pet cat at home.

mcqs.q: A cat likes to:
mcqs.why: A cat likes to eat meat and drink milk. It lives at home because it is a pet animal.

mcqs.q: The name of the pet cat in this lesson is:
mcqs.why: The name of my pet cat is Moti. She likes milk and meat, and I give her food and water every day.

mcqs.q: We take care of a pet by giving it:
mcqs.why: We take care of a pet by giving it food and water every day. The lesson says, "I give her food and water every day."

mcqs.q: A lion is dangerous because it is a:
mcqs.why: A lion is a dangerous wild animal. We cannot play with it and cannot take care of it at home.

mcqs.q: Sana and Ali can keep at home:
mcqs.why: Sana and Ali can keep a cat at home, because a cat is a pet animal that lives at home.

lessons.title: Taking Care of Animals
lessons.notes_html:
What Animals Need

  • Animals need food to eat.
  • Animals need water to drink.
  • Animals need a home for shelter.
  • Animals need our care and love.
  • If we give them these things, animals will stay healthy and happy.

Key Points

  • Animals need food, water, a home, and care and love.

mcqs.q: Animals need ______ to eat.
mcqs.why: Animals need food to eat, water to drink, a home for shelter, and our care and love.

mcqs.q: Animals need ______ to drink.
mcqs.why: Animals need water to drink. They also need food to eat and a home for shelter.

mcqs.q: Animals need a home for:
mcqs.why: Animals need a home for shelter. A home keeps an animal safe, like a nest keeps a bird safe.

mcqs.q: Animals also need our:
mcqs.why: Animals need our care and love. If we give them food, water, a home and care, animals will stay healthy and happy.

mcqs.q: If we give animals these things, they will stay:
mcqs.why: If we give animals food, water, a home and our care and love, animals will stay healthy and happy.

mcqs.q: How many things do animals need in this lesson?
mcqs.why: Animals need four things: food to eat, water to drink, a home for shelter, and our care and love.

mcqs.q: A home keeps an animal:
mcqs.why: Animals need a home for shelter. Shelter means a safe place to live, like a burrow keeps a rabbit safe.

mcqs.q: Animals cannot live without:
mcqs.why: Animals need food to eat and water to drink. Without food and water, no animal can live.

mcqs.q: Shelter means:
mcqs.why: Shelter means a home to live in. Animals need a home for shelter, like birds need a nest.

mcqs.q: To stay healthy and happy, animals need:
options: Food, water, a home and care
mcqs.why: Animals need food, water, a home for shelter, and our care and love. Then they stay healthy and happy.

lessons.title: Importance of Animals
lessons.notes_html:
What We Get from Animals

  • We get eggs from a hen.
  • We get meat from a fish.
  • We go from one place to another place in an animal cart.
  • A goat gives us milk and meat. A cow gives us milk and meat.
  • A camel gives us rides, carries our loads and gives us milk.

Key Points

  • Animals give us food and help us in travel and work.

mcqs.q: We get eggs from a:
mcqs.why: We get eggs from a hen. A hen also gives us meat, and a cow gives us milk and meat.

mcqs.q: We get meat from a:
mcqs.why: We get meat from a fish. A fish eats worms and small water plants and moves by swimming.

mcqs.q: We go from one place to another in an:
mcqs.why: We go from one place to another place in an animal cart. Animals help us in travel also.

mcqs.q: We get milk from a:
mcqs.why: We get milk from a cow. A cow eats grass, moves by walking, and gives us milk and meat.

mcqs.q: A camel gives us:
mcqs.why: A camel gives us rides, carrying of loads and milk. It is a very useful animal.

mcqs.q: We get milk and meat from a:
mcqs.why: We get milk and meat from a goat. A goat eats grass and moves by walking.

mcqs.q: A hen gives us:
mcqs.why: A hen gives us eggs and meat. A hen eats grains and moves by walking.

mcqs.q: A cow gives us:
mcqs.why: A cow gives us milk and meat. A cow eats grass and moves by walking.

mcqs.q: A camel also gives us:
mcqs.why: A camel gives us rides, carrying of loads and milk. So a camel also gives us milk, like a cow and a goat.

mcqs.q: Animals are ______ to us.
mcqs.why: Animals are useful to us. They give us eggs, milk and meat, and they help us in travel and carrying loads.

lessons.title: End of Unit 6 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Revision of Unit 6

  • Flowers are the colourful part at the top of the plant. Roots are under the ground and take in water for the plant.
  • A seed with water and sunlight will grow a lot. A seed with no water and no sunlight will not grow at all.
  • Things given by plants: spices, cotton, wood, vegetables, pencils and fruits. Milk and eggs are NOT given by plants; we get them from animals.
  • Five things made from plants: the quilt (cotton cloth), the wooden cupboard, the wooden door, the wooden bench and the wooden bed.
  • A parrot's home is a nest. A rabbit's home is a burrow. A fish lives in water, a pond or a river.
  • The three things that all living things need to live are food, water and air.

Key Points

  • Grass eaters: cow and goat. Meat eaters: lion and cat.
  • Deer and elephant live in the jungle; cow and horse on the farm; dog and cat at home; fish and duck in a pond; parrot on a tree.

mcqs.q: The colourful and beautiful part at the top of the plant is the:
mcqs.why: Flowers are the colourful and beautiful part, which is at the top of the plant. Roots are under the ground.

mcqs.q: The roots take in ______ for the plant.
mcqs.why: Roots are under the ground and take in water for the plant. The stem is the main long part above the ground.

mcqs.q: A seed given water and sunlight will:
mcqs.why: The plant will grow a lot, because it gets both water and sunlight, the things a plant needs to grow.

mcqs.q: A seed given no water and no sunlight will:
mcqs.why: The plant will not grow at all, because it gets neither water nor sunlight, which a plant must have.

mcqs.q: Which of these is given by plants?
mcqs.why: The things given by plants are spices, cotton, wood, vegetables, pencils and fruits. Milk and eggs are not given by plants; we get them from animals.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT made from plants?
mcqs.why: Bangles are not made from plants. The quilt (cotton cloth), the wooden cupboard, door, bench and bed are made from plants.

mcqs.q: A parrot's home is a:
mcqs.why: A parrot's home is a nest, and a cage when it is kept as a pet. A rabbit's home is a burrow in the ground.

mcqs.q: A fish lives in:
mcqs.why: A fish's home is water, a pond or a river, where it lives and swims. A rabbit lives in a burrow.

mcqs.q: The three things that all living things need to live are:
mcqs.why: The three things that all living things need to live are food, water and air. Every living thing needs these three.

mcqs.q: A deer likes to live in the:
mcqs.why: A deer likes to live in the jungle. An elephant also lives in the jungle, a cow on the farm and a fish in a pond.

lessons.title: Objects Are of Different Sizes
lessons.notes_html:
Big and Small Objects

  • This is a drawing and comparing activity lesson. We draw and compare big and small objects.
  • All objects are not of the same size. Some objects are big and some are small.
  • A watermelon is big. A melon is smaller than a watermelon.
  • An apple is smaller than a melon. A grape is smaller than an apple.
  • An elephant is big and a mouse is small.

Key Points

  • We know the size of an object by comparing it with other objects.
  • Watermelon > melon > apple > grape.

mcqs.q: Are all objects of the same size?
options: No, some are big and some are small
mcqs.why: No, all objects are not of the same size. Some objects are big and some are small, just like an elephant is big and a mouse is small.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the biggest?
mcqs.why: A watermelon is the biggest of these. A melon is smaller than a watermelon, an apple is smaller than a melon and a grape is the smallest.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the smallest?
mcqs.why: A grape is the smallest of these. We draw an apple smaller than the melon and a grape smaller than the apple.

mcqs.q: An elephant is:
mcqs.why: An elephant is big and a mouse is small. Objects are big or small when we compare them with each other.

mcqs.q: A mouse is:
mcqs.why: A mouse is small. An elephant is big. All objects are not of the same size.

mcqs.q: We know the size of an object by:
mcqs.why: All objects are big or small in size when we compare them with each other. Comparison tells us the size.

mcqs.q: A melon is smaller than a:
mcqs.why: In Column B we draw a melon smaller than the watermelon. The watermelon is the biggest fruit in the lesson.

mcqs.q: An apple is smaller than a:
mcqs.why: An apple is smaller than a melon, and a grape is smaller than an apple. Sizes are known by comparing.

mcqs.q: A grape is smaller than an:
mcqs.why: A grape is smaller than an apple. The order from big to small is: watermelon, melon, apple, grape.

mcqs.q: Some objects are big and some are:
mcqs.why: Some objects are big and some are small. All objects are not of the same size.

lessons.title: Objects Are of Different Shapes
lessons.notes_html:
Shapes of Objects

  • A window is square. The top of the table is also square.
  • A warning sign is triangular. The blue object is also triangular.
  • A basket is rectangular. A door is also rectangular.
  • A coin is round. A tennis ball is also round.

Key Points

  • Square: window, table. Triangular: warning sign, blue object.
  • Rectangular: basket, door. Round: coin, tennis ball.

mcqs.q: A window is:
mcqs.why: The window is square and the warning sign is triangular. The top of the table is also square.

mcqs.q: A warning sign is:
mcqs.why: The warning sign is triangular. The blue object in the pictures is also triangular.

mcqs.q: A coin is:
mcqs.why: The coin is round. The tennis ball is also round in shape.

mcqs.q: A door is:
mcqs.why: The door is rectangular. The basket in the pictures is also rectangular.

mcqs.q: A tennis ball is:
mcqs.why: The tennis ball is round, like the coin. Round objects have no corners.

mcqs.q: A basket is:
mcqs.why: The basket is rectangular and the door is also rectangular. The window and the table are square.

mcqs.q: The top of the table is:
mcqs.why: The top of the table is square. The window is also square in shape.

mcqs.q: Which objects are round?
options: The coin and the tennis ball
The warning sign and the blue object
mcqs.why: Round objects are the coin and the tennis ball. Square objects are the window and the table.

mcqs.q: Which objects are square?
options: The coin and the tennis ball
The warning sign and the coin
mcqs.why: Square objects are the window and the table. Rectangular objects are the basket and the door.

mcqs.q: Which objects are triangular?
options: The warning sign and the blue object
mcqs.why: Triangular objects are the warning sign and the blue object. The door and the basket are rectangular.

lessons.title: Objects Have Different Textures
lessons.notes_html:
How Objects Feel

  • This is a touching activity lesson. We touch objects and tell how they feel.
  • A brick is hard.
  • A teddy bear is soft.
  • A tomato is smooth.
  • A stone is rough.
  • In the classroom: the wall is hard, the wooden bench is smooth and our school bag is soft.

Key Points

  • Texture tells us how an object feels when we touch it: hard, soft, smooth or rough.

mcqs.q: A brick feels:
mcqs.why: The brick is hard, the teddy bear is soft, the tomato is smooth and the stone is rough.

mcqs.q: A teddy bear feels:
mcqs.why: The teddy bear is soft. Our school bag in the classroom is also soft to touch.

mcqs.q: A tomato feels:
mcqs.why: The tomato is smooth. The wooden bench in the classroom is also smooth.

mcqs.q: A stone feels:
mcqs.why: The stone is rough. The brick is hard and the teddy bear is soft.

mcqs.q: The wall of the classroom is:
mcqs.why: In the classroom the wall is hard, the wooden bench is smooth and our school bag is soft.

mcqs.q: A wooden bench feels:
mcqs.why: The wooden bench in the classroom is smooth. The wall is hard and the school bag is soft.

mcqs.q: Our school bag feels:
mcqs.why: Our school bag is soft. The wall of the classroom is hard and the wooden bench is smooth.

mcqs.q: We know the texture of an object by:
mcqs.why: We touch the given objects and tell how they feel. Touching tells us if an object is hard, soft, smooth or rough.

mcqs.q: Which of these objects is rough?
mcqs.why: A stone is rough. A tomato and a wooden bench are smooth, and a teddy bear is soft.

mcqs.q: Which of these objects is soft?
mcqs.why: A teddy bear is soft. A brick and a wall are hard, and a stone is rough.

lessons.title: Objects Are of Different Weights
lessons.notes_html:
Heavy and Light Objects

  • This is a comparing activity lesson. We tick the heavier object in each pair.
  • Heavier: an alarm clock than a key; scissors than a paper clip; a cat than a butterfly.
  • Heavier: a car than a bicycle; a potted plant than a pencil; an apple than a strawberry.
  • In a hanger balance, the side with the heavy object goes down and the side with the light object goes up.
  • A stone is heavy and a leaf is light. A pin is light. A marble ball is heavy and a flower is light.

Key Points

  • Small and light objects weigh less than big objects.
  • The heavier side of a balance goes down.

mcqs.q: Which is heavier, a key or an alarm clock?
mcqs.why: The alarm clock is heavier than a key. Small and light objects weigh less than big objects.

mcqs.q: Scissors are heavier than a:
mcqs.why: The scissors are heavier than a paper clip. A paper clip is a very small and light object.

mcqs.q: A cat is heavier than a:
mcqs.why: The cat is heavier than a butterfly. A butterfly is very light, and a car is heavier than a cat.

mcqs.q: A car is heavier than a:
mcqs.why: The car is heavier than a bicycle. A bicycle is lighter than a car.

mcqs.q: A potted plant is heavier than a:
mcqs.why: The potted plant is heavier than a pencil. A pencil is small and light.

mcqs.q: An apple is heavier than a:
mcqs.why: The apple is heavier than a strawberry. A strawberry is smaller and lighter than an apple.

mcqs.q: In a hanger balance, the side with the heavy object goes:
mcqs.why: The side with the stone went down and the side with the leaf went up, so the stone is heavy. The heavy side goes down.

mcqs.q: A stone is ______ than a leaf.
mcqs.why: The side with the stone went down and the side with the leaf went up, so the stone is heavy and the leaf is light.

mcqs.q: A pin is:
mcqs.why: The side with the pin went up and the side with the pen went down, so the pin is light.

mcqs.q: A marble ball is heavier than a:
mcqs.why: The side with the marble ball went down and the side with the flower went up, so the marble ball is heavy and the flower is light.

lessons.title: Objects Are Made of Different Materials
lessons.notes_html:
Metal, Plastic and Wood

  • This is a sorting activity lesson. We sort objects by their material.
  • Metal objects: the screws, the grill and the key.
  • Plastic objects: the beach ball, the grocery bag and the bucket.
  • Wooden objects: the ladder, the wooden box, the rocking horse and the stool.

Key Points

  • Objects are made of different materials: metal, plastic, wood and others.

mcqs.q: Screws are made of:
mcqs.why: Metal objects are the screws, the grill and the key. Plastic objects are the beach ball, the grocery bag and the bucket.

mcqs.q: A key is made of:
mcqs.why: A key is made of metal. The screws and the grill are also made of metal.

mcqs.q: A bucket is made of:
mcqs.why: A bucket is made of plastic. The beach ball and the grocery bag are also plastic objects.

mcqs.q: A grocery bag is made of:
mcqs.why: A grocery bag is made of plastic. The beach ball and the bucket are also made of plastic.

mcqs.q: A ladder is made of:
mcqs.why: A ladder is a wooden object. The wooden box, the rocking horse and the stool are also made of wood.

mcqs.q: A rocking horse is made of:
mcqs.why: A rocking horse is made of wood. The ladder, the wooden box and the stool are also wooden objects.

mcqs.q: A stool is made of:
mcqs.why: A stool is made of wood. Wooden objects in the lesson are the ladder, the wooden box, the rocking horse and the stool.

mcqs.q: A beach ball is made of:
mcqs.why: A beach ball is made of plastic. The grocery bag and the bucket are also plastic objects.

mcqs.q: A grill is made of:
mcqs.why: A grill is made of metal. The screws and the key are also metal objects.

mcqs.q: A wooden box is made of:
mcqs.why: A wooden box is made of wood, as its name tells us. The ladder and the stool are also wooden.

lessons.title: Objects Make Sounds
lessons.notes_html:
How Sounds Are Made

  • A flute makes a sound by blowing.
  • A guitar makes a sound by plucking its strings.
  • A rattle makes a sound by shaking it.
  • A drum makes a sound by beating it.
  • Sound is produced by the vibrations of an object. We hear sounds with our ears.
  • We hear a sound clearly when we are near it. From far away, sound becomes weak.

Key Points

  • Blowing, plucking, shaking and beating make sounds.
  • Sound is made by vibrations and heard by our ears.

mcqs.q: A flute makes a sound by:
mcqs.why: The child with the flute is making a sound by blowing. The boy with the guitar is making a sound by plucking the strings.

mcqs.q: A guitar makes a sound by:
mcqs.why: A guitar makes a sound by plucking its strings. A flute is blown and a drum is beaten.

mcqs.q: A rattle makes a sound by:
mcqs.why: The baby is making a sound by shaking the rattle. A drum is beaten and a flute is blown.

mcqs.q: A drum makes a sound by:
mcqs.why: The boy is making a sound by beating the drum. A rattle is shaken and a guitar is plucked.

mcqs.q: Sound is produced by the ______ of an object.
mcqs.why: Sound is produced by the vibrations of an object. We hear sounds with our ears, so our ears are very important for us.

mcqs.q: We hear sounds with our:
mcqs.why: We hear sounds with our ears. That is why our ears are very important for us.

mcqs.q: Aminah can hear the drum clearly because she is:
mcqs.why: Yes, Aminah can hear the drum clearly because she is standing near the drum. Sound is clear when we are near it.

mcqs.q: Zia cannot hear the drum clearly because he is:
options: Holding his ears shut in the story
mcqs.why: Zia cannot hear the sound clearly because he is standing far away, and sound becomes weak from far away.

mcqs.q: From far away, sound becomes:
mcqs.why: Sound becomes weak from far away. That is why Zia, standing far away, cannot hear the drum clearly.

mcqs.q: Eight glasses filled with water, tapped with a teaspoon, can play:
mcqs.why: Tap each glass gently with a metal teaspoon and it will play the scale: do re mi fa so la ti do.

lessons.title: Some Objects Give Light
lessons.notes_html:
We Need Light to See

  • We cannot see objects clearly at night in the dark, because there is no light.
  • In the day time there is sunlight, so we can see all objects clearly.
  • We need light to see an object.
  • Bright light: a torch, a T.V. and the sun. Dim light: a candle and a lamp.
  • The sun gives the brightest light of all.

Key Points

  • We need light to see things.
  • The sun gives the brightest light.

mcqs.q: We need ______ to see an object.
mcqs.why: We cannot see objects clearly at night in the dark because there is no light. We need light to see an object.

mcqs.q: In the day time, we see objects clearly because of:
mcqs.why: In the day time there is sunlight, so we can see all objects clearly. At night in the dark we cannot see clearly.

mcqs.q: At night in the dark, we cannot see objects:
mcqs.why: We cannot see objects clearly at night in the dark because there is no light there. We need light to see.

mcqs.q: A torch gives:
mcqs.why: A torch gives bright light. A candle and a lamp give dim light, and the sun gives the brightest light of all.

mcqs.q: A candle gives:
mcqs.why: A candle gives dim light. A lamp also gives dim light, while a torch and a T.V. give bright light.

mcqs.q: A lamp gives:
mcqs.why: A lamp gives dim light. A candle also gives dim light. The sun gives the brightest light of all.

mcqs.q: The ______ gives the brightest light of all.
mcqs.why: The sun gives the brightest light of all. A torch and a T.V. give bright light, and a candle gives dim light.

mcqs.q: A T.V. gives:
mcqs.why: A T.V. gives bright light. A torch also gives bright light, but a candle and a lamp give dim light.

mcqs.q: Which of these gives bright light?
mcqs.why: The sun gives bright light; in fact it gives the brightest light of all. A candle and a lamp give dim light.

mcqs.q: Which of these gives dim light?
mcqs.why: A candle gives dim light. The sun, a torch and a T.V. give bright light.

lessons.title: End of Unit 7 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Revision of Unit 7

  • Tennis ball: round, rubber, soft. Window: square, wood, hard. Sign board: triangular, metal, hard.
  • Table: square, wood, smooth. Eraser: triangular, rubber, soft. Coin: round, metal, hard.
  • Door: rectangular, wood, hard. Basket: rectangular, plastic, hard.
  • Two materials: a frying pan has a glass lid and a metal base. An axe has a metal head and a wooden handle. A bulb has a glass round part and a metal base.
  • Yes or No: a stone is not smooth, it is rough. A feather is light. A ball is round. A coin is made of metal, not wood. A stone is hard.
  • A pencil is long and thin, small in size, made of wood with a lead inside it.

Key Points

  • Every object has a shape, a material and a texture.
  • A maraca makes sound by shaking; a guitar by plucking; a drum by beating; a flute by blowing.

mcqs.q: A tennis ball is:
options: Square, made of wood and hard
Triangular, made of metal and hard
Rectangular, made of plastic and hard
Round, made of rubber and soft
mcqs.why: A tennis ball is round in shape, made of rubber in material and soft in texture, as given in the table of this exercise.

mcqs.q: A coin is made of:
mcqs.why: A coin is round, made of metal and hard. A coin is not made of wood.

mcqs.q: An eraser is:
mcqs.why: An eraser is triangular in shape, made of rubber in material and soft in texture, as given in the table.

mcqs.q: The lid of a frying pan is made of:
mcqs.why: The lid of the frying pan is made of glass and its base is made of metal. One object can be made of two materials.

mcqs.q: The handle of an axe is made of:
mcqs.why: The head of the axe is made of metal and its handle is made of wood. The two parts are made of two materials.

mcqs.q: The head of an axe is made of:
mcqs.why: The head of the axe is made of metal and its handle is made of wood, as told in this exercise.

mcqs.q: Is a stone smooth?
mcqs.why: No, a stone is not smooth, it is rough. A stone is hard, and a feather is light.

mcqs.q: A feather is:
mcqs.why: Yes, a feather is very light. A ball is round and a stone is hard and rough.

mcqs.q: A pencil has ______ inside it.
mcqs.why: A pencil is long and thin in shape and small in size. A pencil is made of wood and it has a lead inside it.

mcqs.q: A maraca makes a sound by:
mcqs.why: A maraca makes a sound by shaking it. A guitar makes sound by plucking, a drum by beating and a flute by blowing.

lessons.title: The Weather
lessons.notes_html:
Kinds of Weather

  • Sunny day: the sun is shining, everything looks bright and golden, and we feel hot.
  • Cloudy day: the sun is hiding in the clouds, the sky looks cloudy, and we feel cool and pleasant.
  • Rainy day: rain is falling from the sky, the land is getting wet, and we feel wet and cool.
  • Windy day: the wind is blowing fast, the trees are bending, and we feel cool.
  • Weather words: rainy, fine, cloudy, hot, windy, snowy, sunny, weather.

Key Points

  • The weather can be sunny, cloudy, rainy or windy.

mcqs.q: On a sunny day, we feel:
mcqs.why: On a sunny day the sun is shining and everything looks bright and golden. It is a sunny day and we feel hot.

mcqs.q: On a cloudy day, the sun is:
options: Not in the sky at all
mcqs.why: On a cloudy day the sun is hiding in the clouds and the sky looks cloudy. We feel cool and pleasant.

mcqs.q: On a rainy day, the land gets:
mcqs.why: On a rainy day rain is falling from the sky and the land is getting wet. We feel wet and cool.

mcqs.q: On a windy day, the trees:
mcqs.why: On a windy day the wind is blowing fast and the trees are bending. We feel cool on a windy day.

mcqs.q: On a cloudy day, we feel:
mcqs.why: On a cloudy day the sun is hiding in the clouds. We feel cool and pleasant on such a day.

mcqs.q: On a rainy day, we feel:
mcqs.why: On a rainy day rain is falling and the land is getting wet. We feel wet and cool on a rainy day.

mcqs.q: The sun shines brightly on a:
mcqs.why: On a sunny day the sun is shining over the land and the fields and everything looks bright and golden.

mcqs.q: Rain falls from the sky on a:
mcqs.why: On a rainy day rain is falling from the sky. On a sunny day the sun shines and on a windy day the wind blows.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a weather word?
mcqs.why: Snowy is a weather word. The weather words in the word-search are rainy, fine, cloudy, hot, windy, snowy, sunny and weather.

mcqs.q: On a windy day, we feel:
mcqs.why: On a windy day the wind is blowing fast and the trees are bending. We feel cool on a windy day.

lessons.title: Predicting the Weather
lessons.notes_html:
Guessing the Weather

  • Predicting the weather means telling the weather before time.
  • Today the weather is sunny and hot, and I am feeling well and fresh.
  • I think the weather will be sunny tomorrow too, because the sky is clear today.
  • A model chart for the week: Monday sunny, Tuesday sunny, Wednesday cloudy, Thursday rainy, Friday windy, Saturday sunny, Sunday sunny.
  • Knowing the weather before time helps us decide how to dress and plan what to do.

Key Points

  • We guess tomorrow's weather by looking at the sky today.
  • Weather news helps us dress and plan.

mcqs.q: Predicting the weather means:
mcqs.why: Predicting the weather means guessing and telling the weather before time, like guessing the weather for the coming week.

mcqs.q: If the sky is clear today, tomorrow may be:
mcqs.why: I think the weather will be sunny tomorrow too, because the sky is clear today. A clear sky tells us about sunny weather.

mcqs.q: Knowing the weather before time helps us to:
mcqs.why: Knowing the weather before time helps us decide how to dress and plan what to do.

mcqs.q: Knowing the weather before time also helps us to:
mcqs.why: Knowing the weather before time helps us decide how to dress and plan what to do for the coming days.

mcqs.q: In the model chart, Monday is:
mcqs.why: A model chart: Monday sunny, Tuesday sunny, Wednesday cloudy, Thursday rainy, Friday windy, Saturday sunny, Sunday sunny.

mcqs.q: In the model chart, Thursday is:
mcqs.why: In the model chart, Thursday is rainy. Wednesday is cloudy and Friday is windy in the chart.

mcqs.q: We make a weather chart for:
options: Only one day of last week
mcqs.why: We guess the weather for the coming week, Monday to Sunday, and make a chart of it.

mcqs.q: In the model answer, today's weather is:
mcqs.why: I am feeling well and fresh today and the weather is sunny and hot today, as told in the model answer.

mcqs.q: In the model answer, the child is feeling:
mcqs.why: The child says, "I am feeling well and fresh today." The weather is sunny and hot today.

mcqs.q: We guess tomorrow's weather by looking at:
mcqs.why: I think the weather will be sunny tomorrow because the sky is clear today. We guess the weather by looking at the sky.

lessons.title: The Seasons
lessons.notes_html:
The Four Seasons

  • There are four seasons in a year: Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter.
  • In spring, new leaves and flowers grow.
  • In summer, it is hot. We drink cold water and eat ice-cream.
  • In autumn, the leaves of trees turn yellow and fall down.
  • In winter, it is cold and we wear warm clothes.

Key Points

  • Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter are the four seasons.
  • Summer is the hottest and winter is the coldest season.

mcqs.q: How many seasons are there in a year?
mcqs.why: The four seasons of the year are Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter. Each season is different.

mcqs.q: New leaves and flowers grow in:
mcqs.why: In spring new leaves and flowers grow. In autumn the leaves turn yellow and fall down.

mcqs.q: The hottest season is:
mcqs.why: In summer it is hot, we drink cold water and eat ice-cream. Summer is the hottest season.

mcqs.q: In summer, we eat:
mcqs.why: In summer it is hot, we drink cold water and eat ice-cream to feel cool.

mcqs.q: In autumn, the leaves of trees:
mcqs.why: In autumn the leaves of trees turn yellow and fall down. In spring new leaves and flowers grow.

mcqs.q: In winter, we wear:
mcqs.why: In winter it is cold and we wear warm clothes to keep our bodies warm.

mcqs.q: The coldest season is:
mcqs.why: Winter is the coldest season. In winter it is cold and we wear warm clothes.

mcqs.q: In summer, we drink:
mcqs.why: In summer it is hot, we drink cold water and eat ice-cream. Cold water makes us feel cool.

mcqs.q: Flowers bloom in the ______ season.
mcqs.why: In spring new leaves and flowers grow. Spring is the season of new flowers.

mcqs.q: Leaves turn yellow and fall in the ______ season.
mcqs.why: In autumn the leaves of trees turn yellow and fall down. This is the sign of the autumn season.

lessons.title: End of Unit 8 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Revision of Unit 8

  • Spring things: a watering can, a blossom branch, a sprouting seed.
  • Summer things: a beach ball and bucket, an umbrella, a rain cloud with lightning, an ice-cream.
  • Autumn thing: a basket of fruit. Winter things: skiing, a snowman.
  • Weather table: Sunny day — light cotton clothes, cold drinks and ice-cream, we feel hot. Rainy day — a raincoat and an umbrella, hot pakoras and tea, we feel wet and cool.
  • Cloudy day — normal clothes, warm food, we feel cool and pleasant. Windy day — clothes that cover the body, we feel cool.

Key Points

  • Summer is the hottest season and winter is the coldest.
  • New flowers bloom in spring; leaves fall in autumn.

mcqs.q: A snowman is matched with the ______ season.
mcqs.why: A snowman is matched with winter. Skiing is also a winter thing, and an ice-cream is a summer thing.

mcqs.q: An ice-cream is matched with the ______ season.
mcqs.why: An ice-cream is matched with summer. A beach ball and bucket, an umbrella and a rain cloud are also summer things in the exercise.

mcqs.q: A blossom branch is matched with the ______ season.
mcqs.why: A blossom branch is matched with spring. A watering can and a sprouting seed are also spring things.

mcqs.q: A basket of fruit is matched with the ______ season.
mcqs.why: A basket of fruit is matched with autumn, because autumn is the fruit harvest time in the exercise.

mcqs.q: On a rainy day, we wear:
options: A raincoat and take an umbrella
mcqs.why: On a rainy day we wear a raincoat and take an umbrella, eat hot pakoras and tea, and feel wet and cool.

mcqs.q: On a sunny day, we wear:
mcqs.why: On a sunny day we wear light cotton clothes, take cold drinks and ice-cream, and feel hot.

mcqs.q: On a rainy day, we like to eat:
mcqs.why: On a rainy day we eat hot pakoras and drink tea. On a sunny day we take cold drinks and ice-cream.

mcqs.q: The picture of flowering bushes shows the ______ season.
mcqs.why: Under the picture of flowering bushes we write "Spring". Under the snow scene we write "Winter".

mcqs.q: The picture of a snow scene shows the ______ season.
mcqs.why: Under the snow scene picture we write "Winter". Fallen orange leaves show autumn and people at a river show summer.

mcqs.q: On a cloudy day, we feel:
mcqs.why: On a cloudy day we wear normal clothes, eat warm food and feel cool and pleasant, as given in the weather table.

lessons.title: Means of Transport
lessons.notes_html:
How We Travel

  • Sana and Ali go to school by bus. Their parents go to work by car.
  • Uncle came from Lahore by train. Father will go to Dubai by aeroplane.
  • Vehicles: car, bicycle, donkey cart, train, van, truck, ship, aeroplane and rickshaw.
  • Fast vehicles: car, train, van, truck, aeroplane and rickshaw. Slow vehicles: bicycle, donkey cart and ship.
  • The aeroplane moves the fastest of all.

Where Vehicles Travel

  • Buses travel on the road and stop at the bus stop.
  • Trains travel on railway tracks and stop at the railway station.
  • Aeroplanes travel in the sky and land at the airport.
  • Ships travel in the sea and dock at the harbour.

Key Points

  • Buses stop at the bus stop to pick up and drop off people.

mcqs.q: Sana and Ali go to school by:
mcqs.why: Sana and Ali go to school by bus. Their parents go to work by car.

mcqs.q: Their parents go to work by:
mcqs.why: Their parents go to work by car. Uncle came from Lahore by train.

mcqs.q: Uncle came from Lahore by:
mcqs.why: Uncle came from Lahore by train, and the family went to the station to receive him.

mcqs.q: Father will go to Dubai by:
mcqs.why: Father will go to Dubai by aeroplane next week. Aeroplanes travel in the sky.

mcqs.q: The fastest vehicle of all is the:
mcqs.why: The aeroplane moves the fastest of all. Cars, trains, vans and trucks are also fast vehicles.

mcqs.q: A bicycle moves:
mcqs.why: Slow vehicles are a bicycle, a donkey cart and a ship. A bicycle moves slowly.

mcqs.q: A donkey cart moves:
mcqs.why: A donkey cart is a slow vehicle, like a bicycle and a ship. An aeroplane is the fastest of all.

mcqs.q: Buses stop to pick up and drop off people at the:
mcqs.why: Buses stop at the bus stop to pick up and drop off people. Passengers should also wait for the bus at the bus stop.

mcqs.q: Trains travel on:
mcqs.why: Trains travel on railway tracks and they start and stop at the railway station.

mcqs.q: Ships travel in the:
mcqs.why: Ships travel in the sea and they sail from and dock at the harbour. Aeroplanes travel in the sky.

lessons.title: Traffic Rules
lessons.notes_html:
The Traffic Lights

  • The red light means: Stop.
  • The yellow light means: Wait and get ready.
  • The green light means: Go now.
  • On the signal, the top circle is red, the middle circle is yellow and the bottom circle is green.
  • We must always obey the traffic rules, otherwise we or others may get hurt.

Safety Rules on the Road

  • Look to the right and left and then again to the right before crossing the road.
  • Cross the road at the zebra crossing.
  • Hold the hand of an older person when crossing the road.
  • Wait for the bus at the bus stop. Walk on the footpath.

Key Points

  • Red — Stop. Yellow — Wait. Green — Go.

mcqs.q: The red light means:
mcqs.why: The red light means: Stop. The yellow light means: Wait and get ready. The green light means: Go now.

mcqs.q: The yellow light means:
mcqs.why: The yellow light means: Wait and get ready. The red light means stop and the green light means go.

mcqs.q: The green light means:
mcqs.why: The green light means: Go now. We must always obey the traffic rules, otherwise we or others may get hurt.

mcqs.q: The top circle of the traffic signal is:
mcqs.why: The top circle of the signal is coloured red, the middle circle is yellow and the bottom circle is green.

mcqs.q: The bottom circle of the traffic signal is:
mcqs.why: The bottom circle of the signal is green. Red is at the top for stop, and green is at the bottom for go.

mcqs.q: Before crossing the road, we should look:
options: Right and left, then right again
mcqs.why: Look to the right and left and then again to the right before crossing the road. This is the first safety rule.

mcqs.q: We should cross the road at the:
mcqs.why: Cross the road at the zebra crossing. Crossing at the zebra crossing keeps us safe.

mcqs.q: A child should hold the hand of ______ when crossing the road.
mcqs.why: Hold the hand of an older person when crossing the road. This is one of the five safety rules in the book.

mcqs.q: We should wait for the bus at the:
mcqs.why: Wait for the bus at the bus stop. Buses stop at the bus stop to pick up and drop off people.

mcqs.q: We should walk on the:
mcqs.why: Walk on the footpath. Walking on the footpath keeps us safe from vehicles on the road.

lessons.title: End of Unit 9 Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Revision of Unit 9

  • Aeroplanes fly in the sky. Ships sail in the sea.
  • Trains run on railway tracks. Motorbikes move on the road.
  • Aeroplanes take off and land at the airport. Buses stop at the bus stop.
  • Trains arrive at and leave from the railway station. Ships sail from and dock at the harbour.

Road Signs

  • A line over P: No Parking. A line over a U-turn: No U-Turn.
  • A line over a horn: Do Not Blow Horn. A line over a left arrow: Do Not Turn Left.
  • Children in a triangle: Children Crossing — go slow. An empty red circle: No Entry.

Key Points

  • "This light says Stop" — Red. "Wait" — Yellow. "Go" — Green.

mcqs.q: Aeroplanes fly in the:
mcqs.why: Aeroplanes fly in the sky. Ships sail in the sea and trains run on railway tracks.

mcqs.q: Ships sail in the:
mcqs.why: Ships sail in the sea. They sail from and dock at the harbour.

mcqs.q: Trains run on:
mcqs.why: Trains run on railway tracks. Motorbikes move on the road.

mcqs.q: Aeroplanes take off and land at the:
mcqs.why: Aeroplanes take off and land at the airport. Buses stop at the bus stop and trains at the railway station.

mcqs.q: Trains arrive at and leave from the:
mcqs.why: Trains arrive at and leave from the railway station. Ships sail from and dock at the harbour.

mcqs.q: Ships sail from and dock at the:
mcqs.why: Ships sail from and dock at the harbour. Aeroplanes take off and land at the airport.

mcqs.q: "This light says Stop" — which colour is it?
mcqs.why: "This light says Stop" is the red light. "This light says Wait" is yellow and "This light says Go" is green.

mcqs.q: The sign with a line over the letter P means:
mcqs.why: The sign with a red circle and line over P means No Parking. Parking a vehicle here is not allowed.

mcqs.q: The sign of children in a triangle means:
mcqs.why: The sign of children in a triangle means Children Crossing. School children cross the road ahead, so go slow.

mcqs.q: An empty red circle sign means:
mcqs.why: An empty red circle with a line means No Entry. Going inside on this road is not allowed.
